case_title: PC connected to the wrong access VLAN
symptom: Finance PC cannot reach its Finance gateway or peers; it receives/uses an address for another segment.
topology_note: PC-PT Fa0 to 2960 Fa0/2; Finance VLAN 10 uses router gateway 192.168.10.1.
show_commands: S1# show vlan brief; S1# show running-config interface fa0/2; PC> ipconfig /all
show_output: Fa0/2 appears in VLAN 20; PC is expected in VLAN 10.
expected_fault: Switchport Fa0/2 is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10.
expected_fix: On S1: interface fa0/2; switchport mode access; switchport access vlan 10. Renew/reconfigure the PC address if needed.

case_title: Required user VLAN is missing from the switch
symptom: Engineering PCs on Fa0/3-Fa0/4 are isolated even though their ports reference VLAN 30.
topology_note: Two PC-PT devices on 2960 ports Fa0/3 and Fa0/4; intended VLAN 30 and gateway 192.168.30.1.
show_commands: S1# show vlan brief; S1# show running-config interface fa0/3
show_output: show vlan brief has no VLAN 30; Fa0/3 configuration contains switchport access vlan 30.
expected_fault: VLAN 30 was deleted or never created on the switch.
expected_fix: Create it with vlan 30; name ENGINEERING; then confirm both access ports are assigned to VLAN 30.

case_title: Inter-switch link is configured as an access port
symptom: VLAN 10 hosts on different 2960 switches cannot communicate, while same-switch hosts work.
topology_note: S1 Fa0/24 connected to S2 Fa0/24; VLAN 10 has a PC on each switch.
show_commands: S1# show interfaces trunk; S1# show running-config interface fa0/24; S2# show interfaces trunk
show_output: No operational trunks are listed; Fa0/24 is configured with switchport mode access.
expected_fault: The inter-switch uplink is access mode rather than an 802.1Q trunk.
expected_fix: Configure both uplink ports: switchport mode trunk; optionally set switchport trunk native vlan 99 consistently. Verify with show interfaces trunk.

case_title: VLAN is excluded from the allowed trunk list
symptom: A VLAN 40 PC can reach its local gateway but not a VLAN 40 server across the switch uplink.
topology_note: S1 and S2 trunk on Fa0/24; VLAN 40 PC on S1 and VLAN 40 server on S2.
show_commands: S1# show interfaces trunk; S2# show interfaces trunk
show_output: Fa0/24 is trunking, but VLANs allowed/active show 10,20,30 and omit 40.
expected_fault: VLAN 40 is not allowed across the trunk.
expected_fix: On the relevant trunk: switchport trunk allowed vlan add 40. Confirm VLAN 40 is allowed and forwarding at both ends.

case_title: Host has an address from the wrong subnet
symptom: PC cannot ping its default gateway and is assigned 192.168.20.50 while connected to the 192.168.10.0/24 LAN.
topology_note: PC-PT to 2960 to R1 G0/0; LAN gateway is 192.168.10.1/24.
show_commands: PC> ipconfig /all; PC> ping 192.168.10.1; R1# show ip interface brief
expected_fault: Static host IP belongs to a different subnet.
expected_fix: Set the PC to an unused 192.168.10.x address with mask 255.255.255.0, or use the correct DHCP pool.

case_title: Host subnet mask is too broad
symptom: PC reaches local addresses but sends traffic for 192.168.11.0/24 directly instead of through the gateway.
show_commands: PC> ipconfig /all; PC> tracert 192.168.11.10; R1# show ip route
show_output: PC mask is 255.255.0.0; tracert does not use 192.168.10.1 as first hop.
expected_fault: Host subnet mask is /16 instead of the LAN /24.
expected_fix: Configure mask 255.255.255.0 on the PC and retain gateway 192.168.10.1; retry the trace.

case_title: Host has an incorrect default gateway
symptom: PC can ping same-subnet peers but cannot reach a remote server.
topology_note: PC-PT and R1 G0/0 on 192.168.10.0/24; remote server on 192.168.20.0/24.
show_commands: PC> ipconfig /all; PC> ping 192.168.10.1; PC> tracert 192.168.20.10
show_output: PC gateway is 192.168.10.254, while R1 interface/gateway is 192.168.10.1.
expected_fault: The PC default gateway is not the router interface on its subnet.
expected_fix: Set the PC default gateway to 192.168.10.1 and verify a remote ping.

case_title: Duplicate static IP address
symptom: Two PCs intermittently lose connectivity and ARP resolves the same IP to changing MAC addresses.
topology_note: Two PC-PT devices on one 2960 access VLAN 10, with R1 gateway 192.168.10.1.
show_commands: PC-A> ipconfig /all; PC-B> ipconfig /all; PC-A> ping 192.168.10.60; PC-A> arp -a
show_output: Both PCs are configured as 192.168.10.60/24; the ARP MAC for .60 changes after traffic.
expected_fault: Two endpoints use the same static IPv4 address.
expected_fix: Assign one PC a unique unused address (or DHCP), clear/refresh ARP, and confirm unique addressing.

case_title: DHCP service is disabled on the server
symptom: New clients remain at 0.0.0.0 or APIPA-style addressing and cannot join the LAN.
topology_note: PC-PT to 2960 to Server-PT; server DHCP service supplies 192.168.50.0/24.
show_commands: PC> ipconfig /all; Server-PT Services > DHCP; R1# show ip dhcp binding
show_output: PC has no valid lease; the Server-PT DHCP service toggle is Off; router has no bindings.
expected_fault: The DHCP service is disabled.
expected_fix: Enable DHCP on Server-PT Services > DHCP, ensure the pool is enabled, then renew the PC lease.

case_title: DHCP pool advertises the wrong default gateway
symptom: Client receives a valid IP lease but cannot reach any remote subnet.
topology_note: Server-PT DHCP server on 192.168.60.0/24; R1 G0/0 is 192.168.60.1.
show_commands: PC> ipconfig /all; Server-PT Services > DHCP; PC> ping 192.168.60.1
show_output: PC lease is 192.168.60.50/24 but gateway option is 192.168.60.254; the router is .1.
expected_fault: DHCP pool default-router option is incorrect.
expected_fix: Change the pool default gateway/default-router to 192.168.60.1, save, then release and renew the client lease.

case_title: DHCP pool has no available addresses
symptom: Additional clients fail to obtain addresses while earlier clients retain working leases.
topology_note: Server-PT DHCP pool 192.168.70.0/24 deliberately limited to two assignable addresses; three PCs.
show_commands: Server-PT Services > DHCP; PC-3> ipconfig /all; R1# show ip dhcp binding
show_output: All configured pool addresses are leased; PC-3 has no valid lease.
expected_fault: The DHCP scope is exhausted.
expected_fix: Increase the pool range or reduce lease use, avoiding reserved gateway/static addresses; renew the affected client.

case_title: Router DHCP pool has the wrong network statement
symptom: Client receives no lease from a router acting as DHCP server despite an up LAN interface.
topology_note: R1 G0/0 192.168.80.1/24 to 2960 and PC-PT; R1 provides DHCP.
show_commands: R1# show running-config | section dhcp; R1# show ip dhcp pool; PC> ipconfig /all
show_output: Pool network is 192.168.81.0 255.255.255.0 while G0/0 is 192.168.80.1/24; no binding appears.
expected_fault: Router DHCP pool network does not match the client LAN.
expected_fix: Correct the pool network to 192.168.80.0 255.255.255.0, exclude infrastructure IPs, and renew the client.

case_title: DHCP supplies an unreachable DNS server
symptom: Client can ping the web server IP but cannot browse or ping it by hostname.
topology_note: PC receives DHCP on 192.168.90.0/24; DNS Server-PT is 192.168.90.10.
show_commands: PC> ipconfig /all; PC> ping 192.168.90.10; PC> nslookup intranet.local
show_output: PC DNS server is 192.168.90.99; .99 does not respond, though .10 is the DNS server.
expected_fault: DNS server option on the host/DHCP pool is wrong.
expected_fix: Set the DHCP DNS server option (or static client DNS) to 192.168.90.10, renew the lease, and retest the name.

case_title: DNS A record for internal site is missing
symptom: The intranet server is reachable by IP address but intranet.local cannot be resolved.
topology_note: PC and DNS/Web Server-PT on one routed network; intended A record intranet.local -> 10.10.10.10.
show_commands: PC> nslookup intranet.local; PC> ping 10.10.10.10; Server-PT Services > DNS
show_output: nslookup reports no record for intranet.local; ping to 10.10.10.10 succeeds; DNS service is enabled.
expected_fault: Required DNS A record is absent.
expected_fix: Add A record intranet.local with address 10.10.10.10 on Server-PT, then query the name again.

case_title: DNS service is disabled
symptom: All name lookups fail, although clients can reach the DNS server by IP.
topology_note: PC-PT and Server-PT on 10.10.20.0/24; Server-PT hosts DNS records.
show_commands: PC> ping 10.10.20.10; PC> nslookup portal.local; Server-PT Services > DNS
show_output: Ping to 10.10.20.10 succeeds; DNS service toggle is Off; queries time out/fail.
expected_fault: DNS service is disabled on the server.
expected_fix: Enable DNS on Server-PT Services > DNS and verify existing records before retrying nslookup.

case_title: Static route to remote LAN is missing
symptom: Hosts on R1 LAN cannot reach hosts behind R2, despite an up serial/Ethernet transit link.
show_commands: R1# show ip route; R1# show ip interface brief; PC1> tracert 192.168.2.10
show_output: R1 route table contains connected networks only; no route to 192.168.2.0/24; transit interfaces are up/up.
expected_fault: R1 lacks a route to the R2 LAN.
expected_fix: Add ip route 192.168.2.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.12.2 on R1 and ensure R2 has a return route.

case_title: Static route points to an invalid next hop
symptom: Traffic to a remote network fails at R1 even though a static route is present.
topology_note: R1 and R2 connected on 10.0.12.0/30; R2 serves 172.16.2.0/24.
show_commands: R1# show ip route 172.16.2.0; R1# show running-config | include ^ip route; PC> tracert 172.16.2.10
show_output: Route reads S 172.16.2.0/24 via 10.0.12.6; .6 is not R2 on the transit subnet.
expected_fault: Static route uses the wrong next-hop address.
expected_fix: Remove the bad route and add ip route 172.16.2.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.12.2; verify return routing.

case_title: Edge router has no default route
symptom: Internal clients reach internal networks but cannot reach an ISP test server.
topology_note: R1 LAN 192.168.100.0/24 to ISP router over 203.0.113.0/30; server beyond ISP.
show_commands: R1# show ip route; R1# show running-config | include ^ip route; PC> tracert 198.51.100.10
show_output: R1 has connected LAN and WAN routes but no Gateway of last resort/default route.
expected_fault: Default route toward the ISP is missing.
expected_fix: Configure ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.2 on R1 and validate ISP return routing/NAT as applicable.

case_title: Router LAN interface is administratively down
symptom: Every host on one LAN loses its gateway and remote connectivity after an interface change.
topology_note: PC-PT through 2960 to R1 G0/1, addressed 192.168.110.1/24.
show_commands: R1# show ip interface brief; R1# show running-config interface g0/1; PC> ping 192.168.110.1
show_output: G0/1 shows 192.168.110.1 with Status administratively down and Protocol down.
expected_fault: The LAN router interface has been shut down.
expected_fix: Enter interface g0/1 and issue no shutdown; verify status up/up and test gateway ping.

case_title: OSPF advertises the wrong LAN network
symptom: R2 does not learn R1 LAN route, while the inter-router adjacency is up.
topology_note: R1 and R2 run OSPF area 0 over 10.1.12.0/30; R1 LAN is 10.1.1.0/24.
show_commands: R1# show running-config | section router ospf; R2# show ip route ospf; R1# show ip ospf neighbor
show_output: Neighbor is FULL; R1 OSPF network statement matches 10.1.12.0 but not 10.1.1.0; R2 lacks 10.1.1.0/24.
expected_fault: R1 OSPF configuration does not include its LAN interface network.
expected_fix: On R1 add network 10.1.1.0 0.0.0.255 area 0 (or enable OSPF on G0/0); confirm route appears on R2.

case_title: Inbound ACL blocks approved HTTPS traffic
symptom: Users cannot open the internal HTTPS server, while other allowed services work.
topology_note: Client LAN to R1 to Server-PT 10.20.20.10; extended ACL filters client VLAN inbound.
show_commands: R1# show access-lists; R1# show running-config interface g0/0; PC> ping 10.20.20.10
show_output: ACL contains deny tcp 10.20.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.20.20.10 eq 443 with match counter increasing.
expected_fault: ACL explicitly denies legitimate HTTPS traffic.
expected_fix: Replace/remove the deny and add an appropriate permit tcp rule for HTTPS before any general deny; retest browser access.

case_title: ACL is applied to the wrong interface
symptom: Management workstation cannot reach devices on its local VLAN after an Internet-filter ACL was added.
topology_note: R1 G0/0 is management LAN; G0/1 is WAN; ACL intended for WAN traffic.
show_commands: R1# show running-config interface g0/0; R1# show running-config interface g0/1; R1# show access-lists
show_output: G0/0 has ip access-group INTERNET-FILTER in; G0/1 has none; ACL denies management source traffic.
expected_fault: The ACL is bound inbound on the management LAN interface rather than the intended WAN interface.
expected_fix: Remove ip access-group INTERNET-FILTER in from G0/0 and apply it to the correct interface/direction after policy review.

case_title: ACL direction is reversed
symptom: Traffic initiated by clients is unexpectedly blocked although the ACL entries match the intended client subnet.
topology_note: Client LAN on R1 G0/0, server LAN on G0/1; ACL should filter client traffic near source.
show_commands: R1# show running-config interface g0/0; R1# show running-config interface g0/1; R1# show access-lists
show_output: ACL is applied outbound on G0/0; match counters remain zero while client-to-server packets exit G0/1.
expected_fault: ACL is applied in the wrong direction/interface path.
expected_fix: Remove the misplaced access group and apply it inbound on G0/0 (or outbound on G0/1 according to policy); confirm counters increment correctly.

case_title: PAT is not configured for internal users
symptom: Internal PCs can reach the edge router but cannot reach an external server that lacks routes back to private space.
topology_note: R1 inside LAN 192.168.120.0/24 and outside link 203.0.113.2/30 to ISP server.
show_commands: R1# show ip nat translations; R1# show running-config | section ip nat; PC> tracert 198.51.100.10
show_output: No NAT translations appear after traffic; configuration has no ip nat inside source statement.
expected_fault: NAT/PAT translation rule is missing.
expected_fix: Mark interfaces inside/outside and configure ACL plus ip nat inside source list <acl> interface g0/1 overload; generate traffic and inspect translations.

case_title: NAT inside and outside roles are reversed
symptom: NAT translation table stays empty and Internet access fails after interface role changes.
topology_note: R1 G0/0 faces 192.168.130.0/24; G0/1 faces ISP 203.0.113.2/30; PAT rule exists.
show_commands: R1# show running-config interface g0/0; R1# show running-config interface g0/1; R1# show ip nat translations
show_output: G0/0 is marked ip nat outside and G0/1 is marked ip nat inside, opposite the topology.
expected_fault: NAT inside/outside interface designations are reversed.
expected_fix: On G0/0 use ip nat inside; on G0/1 use ip nat outside; clear translations if needed and test external connectivity.

case_title: NAT ACL omits the user subnet
symptom: One internal VLAN has Internet access but users in VLAN 140 do not.
topology_note: R1 router-on-a-stick: VLAN 130 and VLAN 140; PAT ACL should cover both; one ISP link.
show_commands: R1# show access-lists; R1# show ip nat translations; PC-V140> ping 198.51.100.10
show_output: NAT ACL permits 192.168.130.0/24 only; VLAN 140 packets create no translations.
expected_fault: NAT matching ACL/rule excludes 192.168.140.0/24.
expected_fix: Add permit 192.168.140.0 0.0.0.255 to the NAT ACL (without breaking existing entries); create traffic and confirm a translation.

case_title: Laptop joins the wrong SSID
symptom: Laptop associates to a nearby guest SSID and cannot access required staff resources.
topology_note: Wireless Router/AP broadcasts StaffNet and GuestNet; Laptop-PT should use StaffNet.
show_commands: Laptop-PT Desktop > PC Wireless; Wireless Router GUI > Wireless; Laptop> ipconfig /all
show_output: Laptop wireless profile/association shows GuestNet; StaffNet is the required corporate SSID.
expected_fault: Client selected the wrong SSID.
expected_fix: Select StaffNet in Laptop-PT PC Wireless, use its matching credentials, reconnect, and verify the staff subnet address.

case_title: Wireless security key does not match AP
symptom: Laptop sees StaffNet but authentication/association fails and no IP address is assigned.
topology_note: Laptop-PT connects to Wireless Router/AP StaffNet using WPA2-PSK.
show_commands: Laptop-PT Desktop > PC Wireless; Wireless Router GUI > Wireless Security; Laptop> ipconfig /all
show_output: AP uses WPA2-PSK key Cisco12345; laptop profile has a different key and remains disconnected.
expected_fault: Wireless pre-shared key is incorrect.
expected_fix: Enter the exact WPA2-PSK configured on the AP into the laptop profile, reconnect, then obtain an address.

case_title: Wireless client uses static IP from wrong subnet
symptom: Laptop associates successfully but cannot reach the AP gateway or LAN servers.
topology_note: Wireless Router/AP LAN is 192.168.150.0/24 with gateway 192.168.150.1; Laptop-PT joins StaffNet.
show_commands: Laptop> ipconfig /all; Laptop> ping 192.168.150.1; Wireless Router GUI > Setup
show_output: Laptop is associated but has static 192.168.151.50/24 and gateway 192.168.151.1; AP LAN is 192.168.150.1/24.
expected_fault: Wireless client IPv4 configuration belongs to the wrong subnet.
expected_fix: Set laptop IPv4 to DHCP or a unique 192.168.150.x/24 address with gateway 192.168.150.1; verify gateway ping.

case_title: Guest Wi-Fi can reach an internal server
symptom: Guest laptop successfully pings a protected internal server, violating segmentation policy.
topology_note: Wireless router/AP provides Guest VLAN 160 and Staff/Server VLAN 170; R1 inter-VLAN routing applies policy ACL.
show_commands: Guest Laptop> ping 192.168.170.10; R1# show access-lists; R1# show running-config interface g0/0.160
show_output: Guest ping to 192.168.170.10 succeeds; guest VLAN interface has no ACL blocking 192.168.170.0/24.
expected_fault: Guest wireless VLAN lacks an isolation ACL for the internal server network.
expected_fix: Apply an extended ACL inbound on the guest VLAN interface to deny guest-to-internal traffic while permitting required Internet/DHCP/DNS traffic; verify server ping fails and Internet still works.
